newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanbo's debacle dampens gold demand in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Hanbo's debacle dampens gold demand in Seoul.

text.p: Demand in South Korea's domestic gold market, which had already been dampened by the country's recent labour unrest, was frozen this week on the Hanbo Group's financial debacle, dealers in Seoul said on Tuesday.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group and South Korea's second largest steelmaker, filed for court receivership on Tuesday after it defaulted on debt repayments last week.
"There is no one wanting to buy gold after the financial failure of Hanbo Group," a bullion dealer with Tong Yang Global Corp said.
Other major South Korean financial markets have also been battered by Hanbo's failure, which came as a new body blow to an economy already struggling with a slump in exports.
Despite poor demand, South Korean domestic gold prices were marked up in line with hefty gains in the New York bullion market overnight and the won's weakness against the dollar.

Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, rose by 50 won per gram to 10,120 won from 10,070 won a week ago.
LG's silver price also rose by 10 won a gram to 154 won from 144 won a week earlier.
The won has continuously fallen in line with the yen's weakness against the dollar and on import-related dollar demand.
The won hit 857.5 to the dollar on Seoul's foreign exchange market on Tuesday, the lowest level since the market average system was introduced in March 1990.
Telegraphic transfer selling rates for customer, posted by Korea Exchange Bank, rose to 858.40 won against the dollar from 852.90 a week ago.
The rates are regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for companies.
